name: new-window
covers: File > New Window opens a second, fully loaded window that closes on the first click (Windows deadlock fixed in c4d9c5e). Ctrl+N goes through the same new_window command, but bad-ass-mcp can't send chords on macOS/Windows, so the menu path stands in for it. macOS is skipped: its menu bar belongs to the app, not the window, so window-scoped lookups can't reach it.

phases.note: Windows: the native menu bar's 'File' is in the tree (role 'menuitem'), but invoking it through UIA doesn't open the popup, and the popup's items aren't under the window. So Windows opens the menu with real keys: F10 focuses the menu bar on File, Down opens it with the first item (New Window) highlighted, Return activates it. Keys go without window_id so they're real input.

checks.manual: In the NEW window (list_windows, the one that isn't $WINDOW): learn_layout {'emoji': {'name': 'Insert emoji'}, 'close': {'name': 'Close', 'role': {'windows': 'button'}}} and both resolve (it loaded, not blank white). Click 'close' once (on Linux the window manager's close button, or xdotool windowclose if it isn't in the tree) and check list_windows shows 1 MarkTheCrab window within 3 s. Windows: verified with exactly these names.

notes: The toolbar also has a group named 'File' (the New/Open/Save buttons), so the Linux menu lookup needs its role. Linux names/roles marked confirm come from docs: fix them on the first Linux run.
